claims.text: The Pt-group nanoscale catalyst has exceptional ethanol-oxidation performance.
Synergy between Pt-rich active sites and adjacent Ni or Co atoms governs the catalyst's ethanol-oxidation performance.
Neighboring Ni or Co atoms induce local lattice strain at Pt-rich sites.
Alloying-induced charge transfer shifts the Pt d-band center.
Modification of the Pt electronic structure tunes the binding energy of *OH.
Modification of the Pt electronic structure tunes the binding energies of partially oxidized carbon or *CHx intermediates.
Optimized intermediate adsorption promotes complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
The proposed alloying effect minimizes CO poisoning.
The proposed alloying effect suppresses nanoparticle sintering.
Reduced poisoning and sintering enhance catalyst durability.
An intermediate transition-metal concentration will maximize ethanol-oxidation current density relative to lower or excessively high concentrations.
An intermediate transition-metal concentration will improve selectivity toward complete oxidation products such as CO2.
An intermediate transition-metal concentration will improve stability over repeated cycling.
Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27 is a Pt-rich benchmark composition known to exhibit good ethanol-oxidation activity.
The proposed mechanism applies under moderate-potential ethanol oxidation in alkaline media.
At very high potentials, in strongly acidic media, or at high temperature, other activation or degradation pathways may dominate.

contradictions.description: The material is described as Pt-rich, but the proposed Pt18Ni26Fe15Co14Cu27 benchmark contains only 18 at.% Pt, less than both Ni and Cu, so the bulk composition is not evidently Pt-rich.
